name: org.machanism.machai:genai-client
description: GenAI Client is a Java 8 library for integrating Machai applications with generative AI services through provider-neutral process and embedding contracts. It resolves provider:model identifiers, manages prompts and instructions, invokes OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Claude, EPAM CodeMie, local YAML tool-dispatch, or no-op providers, and records per-model token usage. It supports text generation, embeddings, reflective registration of Java function tools, reusable prompts and URI resources, ServiceLoader discovery of tool bundles, configurable web search, external MCP servers, project-directory context, and configurable tool-error recovery. The primary domains are generative AI application integration, LLM orchestration, semantic search, agent tool calling, and automated project workflows.

usageContext: Java applications that need provider-independent LLM chat or embedding access
Machai workflows with annotated local tools, prompts, and resources
AI-assisted content generation, semantic search, and project assembly
OpenAI web-search and Model Context Protocol tool integration

constructors.description: Creates an OpenAI Responses API provider. Initialize it with a model and org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator before adding prompts or executing requests.

examples.description: Create, initialize, invoke, and clear a conversation-scoped OpenAI provider. Configure OPENAI_API_KEY in the supplied configurator before initialization.

constructors.description: Creates an Anthropic Claude provider. Initialize it with a Claude model and a configurator containing Anthropic credentials before use.

examples.description: Use an Anthropic provider after the configurator has been populated with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and any optional endpoint or timeout settings.

constructors.description: Creates a local, fail-fast tool dispatcher. With model yaml it interprets the latest prompt as a YAML mapping containing a registered tool name and optional parameters.

examples.description: Install the library as a Maven dependency, register an annotated org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools bundle, then invoke a local tool with a YAML request. No external AI credential is required.

features.name: getProvider
features.description: Parses a Provider:Model identifier, resolves a supported provider by naming convention, constructs it using its public no-argument constructor, initializes it, and returns the common ProcessProvider contract.

examples.description: Use provider resolution rather than directly coupling application code to a vendor implementation. Supply OPENAI_API_KEY through the configurator before requesting the OpenAI provider.

features.name: getEmbeddingProvider
features.description: Resolves and initializes an embedding-capable provider from a Provider:Model identifier or a fully qualified provider class name, enabling vector generation for semantic search and similarity workflows.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.process.provider.EmbeddingProvider embeddings = org.machanism.machai.process.manager.ProcessProviderManager.getEmbeddingProvider("OpenAI:text-embedding-3-small", configurator);
java.util.List<java.lang.Double> vector = embeddings.embedding("Searchable project documentation", 1536L);
examples.description: Configure OPENAI_API_KEY, create an OpenAI embedding provider, and generate a vector for indexing or similarity comparison.

features.name: ProcessProvider lifecycle
features.description: Executes the current provider request using accumulated instructions, prompts, configured capabilities, and provider-specific session state. Call clear after an independent conversation to prevent state reuse.

examples.description: Use the None:log provider to install and exercise the standard lifecycle safely in tests or deployments where AI requests are disabled.

features.name: addTools
features.signature: public abstract void org.machanism.machai.process.provider.ProcessProvider.addTools(org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools tools, java.lang.String[] enabledTools)
features.description: Reflectively registers public methods annotated with org.machanism.machai.process.tools.Tool. Filters, when supplied, are regular expressions matched against fully qualified class-name:tool-name identifiers.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.process.provider.ProcessProvider provider = org.machanism.machai.process.manager.ProcessProviderManager.getProvider("OpenAI:gpt-4o-mini", configurator);
provider.addTools(new com.example.tools.ProjectTools(), new java.lang.String[] { "com\\.example\\.tools\\.ProjectTools:read_.*" });
examples.description: After adding genai-client to the application Maven dependencies and configuring OPENAI_API_KEY, register only read-oriented tools from a local annotated tool bundle.

features.name: FunctionToolsLoader.applyTools
features.signature: public void org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionToolsLoader.applyTools(org.machanism.machai.process.provider.ProcessProvider provider, java.lang.String[] tools, java.lang.Class<?> appClass)
features.description: Discovers FunctionTools implementations through java.util.ServiceLoader, applies SupportedFor compatibility rules, and registers compatible tools, prompts, and resources with the target provider.

examples.description: Package a META-INF/services/org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools descriptor with each tool bundle, then discover and activate all compatible tools during application startup.

features.name: UsageStatistics
features.description: Stores immutable input, cached-input, and output token counts in a synchronized in-memory registry keyed by model, for diagnostic and usage reporting during the current application process.

examples.description: Initialize usage reporting at startup, add a measured interaction, and log a per-model summary.

customizations.name: org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools
customizations.description: Marker SPI for reusable bundles of annotated local tools, prompts, and resources. Implementations are normally published through Java ServiceLoader.

examples.description: Create a public tool bundle and expose a public annotated method. Add com.example.tools.ProjectTools to the standard ServiceLoader descriptor to enable automatic discovery.

customizations.name: org.machanism.machai.process.tools.SupportedFor
customizations.description: Restricts a FunctionTools bundle to compatible application classes; excluded classes override included classes.

examples.snippet:
@org.machanism.machai.process.tools.SupportedFor({ com.example.app.DocumentProcessor.class })
public final class com.example.tools.DocumentTools implements org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools { }
examples.description: Limit a tool bundle to applications represented by the listed class before calling FunctionToolsLoader.applyTools.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.process.provider.ProcessProvider
studs.description: Primary lifecycle boundary for generative-AI process providers: initialization, instructions, prompts, annotated tool registration, execution, project-directory context, error handling, and reset.

examples.description: Program against the common interface so the selected provider can be changed by configuration.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.process.provider.EmbeddingProvider
studs.description: Boundary for providers that initialize with a model and configurator and produce vectors from text with provider-specific dimensionality support.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.process.provider.EmbeddingProvider provider = org.machanism.machai.process.manager.ProcessProviderManager.getEmbeddingProvider("OpenAI:text-embedding-3-small", configurator);
java.util.List<java.lang.Double> vector = provider.embedding("semantic-search record", 1536L);
examples.description: Keep semantic indexing code independent of the concrete embedding SDK.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.process.tools.ToolFunction
studs.description: Functional callback boundary used to execute a registered tool, prompt, or resource from a JSON argument tree and optional runtime context objects.

examples.description: Use the callback contract in a provider extension that registers tools programmatically.

examples.title: Install and run an OpenAI chat request
steps: Add the Maven dependency org.machanism.machai:genai-client:1.4.2 to the application build.
Place OPENAI_API_KEY and optional GENAI_TIMEOUT configuration values in the org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator used by the application.
Resolve OpenAI:gpt-4o-mini with ProcessProviderManager, set instructions and a prompt, call perform, then call clear before a separate conversation.

examples.title: Install, configure, and invoke a local YAML functional tool
steps: Implement org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools with public methods annotated by Tool and Param, or publish the implementation in META-INF/services/org.machanism.machai.process.tools.FunctionTools.
Initialize Tools:yaml, register the bundle, and pass a YAML document whose tool value equals the registered name and whose params mapping contains its input.

examples.title: Configure OpenAI web search and an MCP server
steps: Configure OPENAI_API_KEY for the OpenAI provider.
Set WebSearchTool.type=default to register OpenAI web search; optionally add WebSearchTool.city, WebSearchTool.country, and WebSearchTool.region.
Set MCP.url and MCP.name for an external Model Context Protocol server; optionally set MCP.authorization and MCP.description. Initialize OpenAI:gpt-4o-mini after these settings are available.
examples.configuration:
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-api-key
WebSearchTool.type=default
MCP.url=https://example.org/mcp
MCP.name=Project MCP
MCP.authorization=Bearer your-token
